key_insight: RIDAR detects research integrity violations in autonomous research agents and intervenes during execution to reduce violations remaining at task completion.
engineering_relevance: Research-agent pipelines can use trajectory auditing and runtime intervention to help safeguard validity, reproducibility, and faithful reporting.
method: Define 14 research integrity violation types across the research lifecycle using the RIVT taxonomy.
Audit agent trajectories with RIDAR-post-hoc to detect violations.
Detect and correct violations during execution with RIDAR-runtime.
evidence_signal: RIDAR-post-hoc achieved 85.2% F1 on 60 expert-annotated trajectories and detected 3,964 violations across 99.7% of 300 trajectories covering 50 tasks; runtime intervention reduced remaining violations by 36.8%.
watch_item: Detection is imperfect, and runtime intervention reduces rather than eliminates violations, so independent validation remains necessary.
paper_title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
